newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prod prices flat amid thin markets.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prod prices flat amid thin markets.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products were flat Monday amid relatively flat futures and thin participation amid an industry function, dealers said.
Crude oil for July delivery exteneded last week's late-week rise, rising 18 cents a barrel Monday to $19.01.
Refined product futures were also slightly higher, with heating oil up 0.30 cents a gallon, and unleaded gasoline up 0.63 cents a gallon.
Trade was thin Monday as traders attend a golf tournaments in southern California sponsored by Mobil. Traders also awaited a weekly inventory report on Tuesday.
June supplies of Los Angeles cleaner-burning CARB gasoline stood unchanged at 53/54 cents, while conventional gasoline off 1.50 at 51.50/52.50 cents.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles was flat at 57.50/58.50.
Reformulated gasoline in L.A. and San Francisco was offered at a one cent discount to L.A. CARB gasoline.
